system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A process named pfupdater.exe ran from leo.martins's AppData\Roaming\PixelForge directory, rather than the approved C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe location in the supplied inventory.

That process made recurring connections through the proxy to updates.pixelforge-suite.co, while the supplied approved update domain is updates.pixelforge-suite.com. The observed hostname therefore differs from the approved hostname.

The proxy records show connections to that .co hostname at 13:37:36, 13:42:43, 13:47:14, 13:52:45, 13:57:44, 14:02:11, and 14:07:36 UTC—roughly five-minute intervals. Endpoint network records associate the connections with pfupdater.exe (PID 3992).
The executable and destination mismatch, combined with the regular updater-like connections, is consistent with an unapproved process masquerading as the approved PixelForge updater.
Dropbox.exe and GoogleDriveFS.exe started in leo.martins's user session; the supplied inventory does not approve Dropbox or Google Drive as file-sharing or cloud-storage services.
The logs show pfupdater.exe generating a file-creation event targeting its own executable path; the record does not establish what content was written.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnels to the PixelForge-like hostname, but the provided records do not expose the tunnel's application-layer contents or downloaded payload.
The records provide no hash, signature validation, or file contents for the AppData\Roaming pfupdater.exe.
The Dropbox and Google Drive records show process starts, but the supplied logs do not show whether either process made network connections or transferred data.
A file-creation event targeting pfupdater.exe does not, by itself, establish the file's contents, whether it was replaced, or whether it executed updated code.
claims_not_established: The logs do not establish what data, if any, left the workstation or whether any file-sharing process successfully synchronized data.
The logs do not establish the contents or behavior of the traffic carried inside the HTTPS tunnels.
The logs do not establish who installed the AppData\Roaming executable or whether the mismatched domain was controlled by an attacker.
The records do not establish whether the file-creation event changed the executable.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze the pfupdater.exe file, including cryptographic hashes, signature status, metadata, and comparison with a known-good vendor copy.
Obtain proxy TLS inspection or endpoint network inspection data for the recurring connections, including request paths, certificates, and response or downloaded-file details.
Review endpoint file, download, browser, and installation history to determine how the executable arrived and whether it was modified.
Check endpoint telemetry for Dropbox and Google Drive network activity and file-access or synchronization evidence.
Validate with the software owner or vendor whether updates.pixelforge-suite.co is legitimate or authorized.
